title: A projection-preserving extension linearizes the pinned dyadic fibre phase
statement: There exist a group G, a surjective homomorphism pi:G->F_2^7, and a homomorphism q:G->Z/4 such that q=d composed with pi for the normalized product-discriminant phase d of the pinned degree-eleven dyadic fibre. THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE: d(1)=1 but d(1 xor 1)=0 is not 1+1 modulo four.

formal.statement: {"claim":"exists G, surjective homomorphism pi:G->F_2^7, and homomorphism q=d*pi:G->Z/4","counterexample":{"expected_xor_phase_mod_four":2,"left":1,"left_phase_mod_four":1,"right":1,"right_phase_mod_four":1,"xor_phase_mod_four":0},"fibre":{"dimension":7,"full_support_coefficient_mod_eight":6,"paired_coordinate_shift":48,"polynomial_degree":11},"format":"axeyum-gf2-dyadic-fibre-projection-obstruction","version":1}

evidence.supports: The exact 128-point product-discriminant table has full-support coefficient 6 modulo eight and normalized phase d(1)=1, so d(1 xor 1)=0 differs from d(1)+d(1)=2 modulo four.
evidence.notes: Surjectivity then lifts any pair of quotient coordinates; homomorphism of d composed with pi would force d itself to be additive. The calculation uses exact integer discriminants modulo eight.

provenance.source: native exact product-discriminant table and elementary quotient-homomorphism argument

notes: This rules out only extensions that retain the affine fibre as a homomorphic quotient. It does not rule out a joined nonabelian law that mixes affine, auxiliary, valuation, and Witt coordinates, and it grants no endpoint cancellation credit.
